title: TESS 2-min data of 21,385 Sun-like stars agree with the Kepler superflare rate within a factor of 2, except stars with a co-moving companion within 10 arcsec, which show 24 times more flares
abstract: Question: does TESS confirm the Kepler rate of superflares above 1e34 erg on Sun-like stars (8.6e-3 per star per year; Vasilyev et al. 2024)? Approach: we searched 60,000 randomly selected TESS SPOC 2-min light curves (sectors 1-107) of stars with the Kepler study's Gaia DR3 cuts (4 < M_G < 6, RUWE < 1.4, Teff 5000-6500 K). After rotation and variability cuts, 42,315 star-sectors of 21,385 stars (2,478 star-years) remain. We measured the detection efficiency with 766,885 injected flares and forward-modelled the Kepler rate. We vetted all candidates by eye and with target-pixel difference images, and split the stars by Gaia DR3 neighbours. Findings: at peak >= 8 sigma and E >= 1e34 erg, all stars give 23 flares against 8.8 expected (ratio 2.6, 95% 1.6-3.9; 4.4 for wider flares). Stars without a Gaia neighbour within 42 arcsec give 3 against 3.9 (ratio 0.8-1.3), and stars without a co-moving companion within 10 arcsec give 11 against 8.3 (1.3-2.2). The 5% of stars with a co-moving companion have 12 flares against 0.5 expected (ratio 24, 95% 12-41). For 10 of 11 such flares with a measurable offset, the pixel offset points toward the companion (p = 1.3e-4), so faint M-dwarf companions inside the 21-arcsec pixels produce the excess. Limitations: few flares on clean stars, the efficiency depends on the assumed flare width (10-20 min), TESS cannot apply the Prot > 20 d cut, one analyst did the visual vetting, and companions closer than about 1 arcsec stay unresolved.

display.caption: Observed over expected TESS flares above 1e34 erg (peak >= 8 sigma) for four Gaia neighbour groups. Expected counts use the Vasilyev et al. (2024) Kepler rate and the measured TESS detection efficiency for flare widths of 10 min (blue) and 20 min (orange) at 1e34 erg. Bars are 95% Poisson intervals.

Left: difference-image centroid offsets of flares on stars with a co-moving companion within 10 arcsec, rotated so that the companion is at (1, 0) in units of the separation. Filled points exceed the 95th percentile of an on-target null. Right: offset size against flare peak significance for the three neighbour groups.

Two flares on stars with a co-moving companion (offset arrow, x10, follows the companion direction, dashed) and one flare on a star without neighbours (no offset). Contours show the quiescent star image.
